title: Shepherd of Hermas, Chapter 21
language: Greek (Codex Sinaiticus) / English (J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers)
source: Codex Sinaiticus folio + transcription (codexsinaiticus.org) + J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
description: Shepherd of Hermas chapter 21. Manuscript page scan(s) from Codex Sinaiticus hosted by the Codex Sinaiticus Project, with the Project's verbatim transcription of the Greek and the English of J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891).
introduction:
This entry meets the strict three-criteria standard of the Theosis Library:

  1. Manuscript scan: The actual folio(s) of Codex Sinaiticus containing this chapter, from the Codex Sinaiticus Project (codexsinaiticus.org). Each section links to the specific folio holding its verses.
  2. Original text: The Codex Sinaiticus Project's verbatim transcription of the folio shown (uncial letters, lunate sigma, nomina sacra preserved).
  3. English translation: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891), public domain, retrieved verbatim from Lightfoot 1891 via earlychristianwritings.com transcription.

Numbering: Chapter 21 in the continuous (Whittaker) numbering used by the Codex Sinaiticus Project is Vision 3, chapter 13 in Lightfoot's traditional division, which the English column follows.

Why this is here: Codex Sinaiticus binds this text after Revelation, alongside the canonical books. Reading it on the same parchment as the Gospels is primary evidence for how a 4th-century Christian community treated it.

translation.original_text: <sup>1</sup>τη δε τριτη οραϲει ειδεϲ αυτην νεωτεραν και καλη και ιλαραν και καλην την μορφη αυτηϲ <sup>2</sup>ωϲ εαν γαρ τινι λυπουμενω ελθη αγʼγελια αγα τιϲ ευθυϲ επελαθετο των προτερων λυπων και ουδεν αλλο προϲδεχεται ει μη τη αγγελιαν ην ηκουϲεν και ϊϲχυροποιειται λοιπον ειϲ το αγαθον και ανανεουται αυτου το πνα δια την χαραν ην ελαβεν ουτωϲ και ϋμιϲ ανανεωϲιν ϊληφατε των πνευματων ϋμων ϊδοντεϲ ταυτα τα αγαθα <sup>3</sup>και οτι επι ϲυμψελιου ειδεϲ καθημενη ϊϲχυρα η θεϲειϲ οτι τεϲϲαρεϲ ποδαϲ εχι το ϲυμψελιον και ϊϲχυρωϲ εϲτηκεν και γαρ ο κοϲμοϲ δια τεϲϲαρων ϲτοιχιω κρατιται <sup>4</sup>οι ουν μετανοηϲαντεϲ ολοτελωϲ νεοι εϲονται και τεθεμελιωμενοι εξ οληϲ καρδιαϲ με̣τανοηϲαντεϲ απεχειϲ ολοτελη την αποκαλυψεν μηκαιτη μηδεν ετηϲειϲ εα τι δε δεη αποκαλυφθηϲεται ϲοι
translation.text: <sup>1</sup>But in the third vision ye saw her younger and fair and gladsome, and her form fair. <sup>2</sup>For just as when to some mourner cometh some piece of good tidings, immediately he forgetteth his former sorrows, and admitteth nothing but the tidings which he hath heard, and is strengthened thenceforth unto that which is good, and his spirit is renewed by reason of the joy which he hath received; so also ye have received a renewal of your spirits by seeing these good things. <sup>3</sup>And whereas thou sawest her seated on a couch, the position is a firm on; for the couch has four feet and standeth firmly; for the world too Is upheld by means of four elements. <sup>4</sup>They then that have fully repented shall be young again, and founded firmly, seeing that they have repented with their whole heart. There thou hast the revelation entire and complete. Thou shalt ask nothing more as touching revelation-- but if anything be lacking still, it shall be revealed unto thee."

verification.translator: J. B. Lightfoot, The Apostolic Fathers (1891)
